# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in this repo.

## Project overview

React assessment starter (CarTrawler-style car rental UI). The task (see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`) is to build two **responsive** Storybook components that match the Figma designs:

1. **Car Block** — a single car result card (vehicle details, pricing, policies).
2. **Car List** — a list of Car Blocks rendered from every car in `src/assets/response.json`.

Reviewers weigh _how_ the code is built (clean structure, design-system fidelity, tests, a11y) as much as the result. Prefer small, composable, well-typed components.

The deliverable also requires an `AGENTS.md` at the repo root (instructions for AI agents). Keep it in sync with this file.

## Stack

Vite 8, React 19, TypeScript 5.9 (strict), Storybook 10 (`@storybook/react-vite`), Vitest 5 + Testing Library (jsdom), ESLint 10 flat config + Prettier. Node 24 (`.nvmrc`).

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run dev            # Vite dev server  :5173
npm run storybook      # Storybook        :6006
npm test               # Vitest, single run
npm run test:watch     # Vitest watch
npm run lint           # ESLint (lint:fix to auto-fix)
npm run format         # Prettier write (format:check to verify)
npm run build          # tsc -b && vite build (type-check + bundle)
npm run build-storybook
```

## File map

```
src/
  assets/response.json     # fixture: { productType, searchId, responseTime, cars[], vendors[], locations[] }
  components/              # Counter.* is the example; follow its pattern
    X.tsx / X.css / X.test.tsx / X.stories.tsx
  design-system.css        # tokens + typography utility classes (source of truth for styling)
  App.tsx, main.tsx, index.css
docs/
  adr/                     # architecture decision records (0001 = Car Block / Car List)
  design/<slug>/           # generated Figma specs (spec.md, spec.json, screenshots/)
  plans/                   # development plans written by the architect agent
.claude/skills/figma-spec/ # skill that turns a Figma link into docs/design/<slug>/
.claude/skills/commit/     # skill that commits with the commitlint conventional format
.claude/agents/            # agent definitions (architect, implementer, qa-specialist)
.storybook/                # main.ts (stories glob), preview.ts (imports design-system.css)
vite.config.ts             # Vite + Vitest config, `@` alias
vitest.setup.ts            # jest-dom matchers
commitlint.config.js       # commitlint rules (extends config-conventional)
.husky/commit-msg          # git hook that runs commitlint on every commit
```

## Workflow

1. **Architect** (`.claude/agents/architect.md`) reads the ADR, obtains the Figma spec and writes a detailed development plan to `docs/plans/<slug>.md`.
2. **Human approval gate.** The plan is written as `Status: DRAFT — awaiting human approval`. A human must review it and explicitly approve it or request changes; changes bump `Revision` and keep it DRAFT. Only an explicit approval sets `Status: APPROVED by <name> on <date> (revision <n>)`. Agents never approve a plan themselves; when the architect returns, ask the user to approve or request changes before implementing.
3. **Implementer** (`.claude/agents/implementer.md`) starts only when the plan header reads `APPROVED`, then follows it step by step, building from the local spec and never calling Figma. If the plan changes after approval it returns to DRAFT.
4. **QA specialist** (`.claude/agents/qa-specialist.md`) audits the code against the plan and ADR acceptance criteria, writes success-path tests to reach at least 80% coverage, then starts Storybook and the dev server so a human can compare the result with Figma.
5. **Final human acceptance.** QA leaves `QA Status: AWAITING HUMAN APPROVAL` in the plan. Only the human's explicit approval sets `QA Status: ACCEPTED by <name> on <date>`; reported design differences go back to the implementer as a defect list. The feature is done only when ACCEPTED.
6. Verify against the definition of done below.

There is no user-story step; the ADR acceptance criteria are the requirements.

### Agents (`.claude/agents/`)

| Agent       | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | May edit                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| architect   | Reads the ADR, gets the Figma spec via the `figma-spec` skill, writes the detailed plan as a DRAFT and stops at the approval gate.                                                                                                                | `docs/plans/` only                |
| implementer | Reads an APPROVED plan and builds it with the project standards: tokens-only CSS, colocated component/test/stories, strict TS. Refuses to start on a non-APPROVED plan, never calls Figma, runs lint/test/build/format:check before reporting. | `src/` and the plan's checkboxes  |
| qa-specialist | Feature-agnostic: audits the code against any approved plan and its ADR criteria, writes success-path tests for at least 80% coverage of the changed code (coverage needs `@vitest/coverage-v8`; ask before adding it), runs the app for the human to review (against the design spec when there is one), and waits for final human approval. Never fixes application code. | `*.test.ts(x)` and the plan's QA section |

The implementer stops and reports (instead of deviating) if the plan is wrong or ambiguous; scope or design changes send the plan back to DRAFT for re-approval. Visual fidelity still needs a human check in Storybook.

## Architecture & conventions

- **Imports**: use the `@/` alias for anything under `src/` (`import Counter from "@/components/Counter"`). Relative imports only for same-folder siblings (as in Counter's test/story).
- **Colocation**: each component lives in `src/components/` with its `.css`, `*.test.tsx` and `*.stories.tsx` next to it. Components are exported both named and default (see `Counter.tsx`).
- **Props**: declare a `type XProps` above the component with JSDoc on each prop; Storybook `argTypes` mirror them.
- **Styling**: plain CSS files imported by the component (no CSS-in-JS/Tailwind). Style **only** with design-system tokens — never hard-code colors, px spacing, radii or font sizes if a token exists:
  - Colors: `--text-*`, `--bg-fill-*`, `--border-*`, `--button-*`, `--price-*`, `--surface-*`, `--container-*`, etc.
  - Typography: apply `.ts-display-*`, `.ts-headline-*`, `.ts-subtitle-*`, `.ts-body-*`, `.ts-label-*`, `.ts-button-*` classes.
  - Spacing/sizing: `--space-*`, `--bw-*` (border width), `--br-*` (radius).
  - Breakpoints: mobile 608px, tablet 840px, desktop-small 1025px, desktop-large 1328px. CSS custom properties can't be used inside `@media` conditions, so write the literal px value and note which breakpoint it mirrors in a comment. Design mobile-first (`min-width`).
  - Read exact tokens off Figma; don't guess. Figma: see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
  - **Don't call Figma while building.** Use the `figma-spec` skill (`.claude/skills/figma-spec/`) to extract a Figma link once into `docs/design/<slug>/spec.md` (token-mapped colors, spacing, radii, typography, layout), then build from that file. Reuse an existing spec instead of re-fetching; only refresh if the design changed. Needs `FIGMA_TOKEN` in a git-ignored `.env`; never print or commit it.
- **Types**: model them on `response.json` (`vehicle`, `rentalRates[]` with `pricing`, `deposit`, `fuelPolicy`, `mileagePolicy`, `insuranceCoverage`, `config`). Money values are `{ amount: string, currency: string }` — amounts are strings; format via `Intl.NumberFormat`, don't parse ad hoc. Put shared types in a dedicated types file under `src/`, not inside components. Do not use `any`.
- **TypeScript rules in force**: `strict`, `noUnusedLocals/Parameters`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type` for types), `erasableSyntaxOnly` (no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties).
- **ESLint**: `react-hooks` rules and `react-refresh/only-export-components` (warn) — keep non-component exports out of component files.
- **Formatting** (Prettier): double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 80 cols, 2-space indent. Run `npm run format` rather than hand-formatting.
- **Commits**: Conventional Commits enforced by commitlint (`@commitlint/config-conventional`) through a husky `commit-msg` hook: `type(scope): subject`, lowercase imperative subject, no trailing period, header ≤ 100 chars. Use the `commit` skill (`.claude/skills/commit/`) to stage explicit files, validate and commit; never `--no-verify`, never amend/push unless asked. Packages are installed per the skill's Setup section (needs `git init` and `npm install`).
- **Accessibility**: semantic HTML (lists for the Car List, headings in a sensible order), meaningful `alt` text on car images, visible focus states, keyboard-operable controls.
- **Performance**: `loading="lazy"` on images; memoize only where it measurably matters.

## Testing

- Vitest globals are on, but the existing tests still import `describe/it/expect` from `vitest` — follow that.
- Query by role/text (`getByRole`, `getByText`) first; `data-testid` only as a fallback.
- Use `userEvent.setup()` for interactions.
- Test with the real fixture (or a slice of it) for Car Block / Car List: renders every car, key fields (make/model, price, policies), edge cases (missing optional fields, empty list).

## Storybook

- Title convention: `Components/<Name>`, with `tags: ["autodocs"]` and typed `Meta`/`StoryObj`.
- Cover the happy path plus edge cases: long names, missing image, no insurance, free cancellation vs. fee, empty list, loading/error states for the list.
- Verify responsive behavior with Storybook viewports (mobile/tablet/desktop).

## Definition of done

- Matches Figma at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
- Uses design-system tokens/classes only.
- Stories and colocated unit tests exist for each component.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass cleanly.
- `AGENTS.md` is present and up to date.

## Boundaries — ask before changing

- `src/design-system.css` (read-only source of truth; add local CSS in component files instead).
- `src/assets/response.json` (fixture; build edge cases as story/test data derived from it).
- Tooling config: `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.json`, `commitlint.config.js`, `.husky/*`, `.storybook/*`, `package.json` dependencies.
- Don't add new dependencies without asking. Never commit `node_modules`, `dist` or `storybook-static`.
- `Counter.*` is starter scaffolding; remove it (and its `App.tsx` usage) only as part of replacing it with the real solution.

1	# ADR 0001: Car Block and Car List components
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-10-21
5	- **Deciders:** rhoger.anacleto
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	### Task description
10	
11	Build two React components that render car rental search results, documented
12	in Storybook and covered by unit tests (see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`):
13	
14	1. **Car Block** — a single car result card showing vehicle details, pricing
15	   and policies for one car.
16	2. **Car List** — a list of Car Blocks, one for every car in
17	   `src/assets/response.json`.
18	
19	Constraints:
20	
21	- Both components must be **responsive** across mobile, tablet and desktop.
22	- Figma is the source of truth for layout, spacing and styling.
23	- All styling must come from the design system in `src/design-system.css`
24	  (CSS variables and `.ts-*` utility classes), not ad-hoc values.
25	- Types are modelled on the fixture: each car has a `vehicle` and
26	  `rentalRates[]` (pricing, deposit, cancellation, fuel and mileage policy,
27	  insurance coverage, config flags).
28	- Stack is fixed: React 19, strict TypeScript, Vite, Storybook 10, Vitest +
29	  Testing Library, ESLint + Prettier. Components, tests and stories are
30	  colocated and imported through the `@/` alias.
31	- An `AGENTS.md` for AI agents working in the repo is also required. AI
32	  assistance is encouraged.
33	
34	## Alternatives considered
35	
36	### 1. Styling
37	
38	| Option                                                | Pros                                                                              | Cons                                                                         |
39	| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
40	| **Plain colocated CSS using design-system tokens**    | Matches the `Counter` pattern; tokens and `.ts-*` classes used directly; no deps  | Class naming discipline is manual                                            |
41	| CSS Modules                                           | Scoped class names                                                                | Extra convention not used by the starter; stories and tests need no benefit  |
42	| Tailwind or CSS-in-JS                                 | Fast to write                                                                     | New dependency; duplicates the existing design system; against the brief     |
43	| Inline styles                                         | No stylesheet                                                                     | No media queries or pseudo-states; encourages hard-coded values              |
44	
45	### 2. Component structure
46	
47	| Option                                                       | Pros                                                          | Cons                                    |
48	| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
49	| One monolithic `CarBlock`                                    | Fewest files                                                  | Hard to test, read and reuse            |
50	| **`CarBlock` composed of small presentational sub-components** | Each piece is testable and readable; clean, well-typed props | More files; needs a sensible split      |
51	
52	### 3. Data and types
53	
54	| Option                                                           | Pros                                                       | Cons                                     |
55	| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
56	| Import `response.json` and let TypeScript infer types            | Zero effort                                                | Literal-inferred types; fragile; no docs |
57	| **Dedicated types file modelled on `response.json`**             | Explicit, reusable by components, tests and stories        | Must be kept in sync with the fixture    |
58	
59	`CarBlock` receives a single `Car`; `CarList` receives `Car[]`. Components do
60	not import the JSON themselves, so they stay reusable and easy to feed edge
61	case data.
62	
63	### 4. Responsiveness
64	
65	| Option                                                  | Pros                                                       | Cons                                                              |
66	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| **Mobile-first `min-width` media queries**              | Simple, universal, matches the design-system breakpoints   | `var(--breakpoint-*)` cannot be used in `@media`; literals needed |
68	| Container queries                                       | Component adapts to its container                          | Breakpoints in the design system are viewport-based               |
69	| JS-based breakpoints (`matchMedia` hooks)               | Conditional rendering possible                             | Extra runtime logic, flicker, harder to test                      |
70	
71	### 5. Testing
72	
73	| Option                                                    | Pros                                         | Cons                                       |
74	| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
75	| **Testing Library by role and text, using fixture data**  | Tests behaviour users see; resilient         | Slightly more verbose                      |
76	| Snapshot tests                                            | Quick to write                               | Brittle, low signal, noisy diffs           |
77	
78	### 6. Cars with several `rentalRates`
79	
80	| Option                                                   | Pros                                  | Cons                                           |
81	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
82	| **Render one rate: the one with the best relevance**     | Matches a "single result card" design | Must confirm the rule against Figma and data   |
83	| Render all rates in the block                            | Shows everything                      | Not what the design shows; clutters the card   |
84	
85	## Decision
86	
87	Build `CarBlock` and `CarList` as small, typed, presentational React
88	components styled with plain colocated CSS that uses only design-system
89	tokens, designed mobile-first.
90	
91	### How
92	
93	- **Layout of files** under `src/components/`, following `Counter`:
94	  `CarBlock.tsx`, `CarBlock.css`, `CarBlock.test.tsx`, `CarBlock.stories.tsx`,
95	  and the same four files for `CarList`. Small sub-components (for example
96	  vehicle info, price, policies) live next to `CarBlock` and are composed by
97	  it.
98	- **Types** live in a dedicated types file under `src/`, modelled on
99	  `response.json`. Money values are `{ amount: string; currency: string }`
100	  and are formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`, never parsed ad hoc.
101	- **Styling** uses `var(--token)` and `.ts-*` classes only. Each visual
102	  property is mapped to its token by inspecting Figma. Media queries are
103	  `min-width` with literal px values mirroring `--breakpoint-mobile` (608px),
104	  `--breakpoint-tablet` (840px), `--breakpoint-desktop-small` (1025px) and
105	  `--breakpoint-desktop-large` (1328px), each with a comment naming the token.
106	- **Semantics and accessibility:** `CarList` renders a `<ul>` of `<li>`;
107	  `CarBlock` is an `<article>` with a heading; images have meaningful `alt`
108	  text and `loading="lazy"`; interactive elements are keyboard-operable with
109	  visible focus.
110	- **Rate selection:** show the rental rate with the lowest `orderByRelevance`
111	  (to be confirmed against Figma); cars without rates render a safe fallback
112	  rather than crashing.
113	- **Stories** use title `Components/<Name>` with `autodocs`. They cover the
114	  happy path and edge cases (long names, missing image, no insurance, free
115	  cancellation vs fee, empty list, loading and error states for the list).
116	- **Tests** query by role and text and use the real fixture (or slices of it).
117	  They check that the list renders every car, key fields of a block, and the
118	  edge cases above.
119	
120	### Why
121	
122	- Design-system tokens keep the result consistent with the brand and are an
123	  explicit requirement; hard-coded values would fail review.
124	- Plain CSS adds no dependency and follows the existing starter pattern.
125	- Small composed components keep each unit readable and testable, and show
126	  structural judgment, which the assessment evaluates.
127	- Typing from the fixture makes the data contract explicit and gives
128	  compile-time safety for stories and tests.
129	- Mobile-first media queries are the simplest approach that satisfies the
130	  design-system breakpoints without runtime logic.
131	- Behavioural tests survive refactors; snapshots would not.
132	
133	## Consequences
134	
135	**Positive**
136	
137	- No new dependencies; consistent with `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`
138	  conventions.
139	- Components are reusable and easy to exercise from Storybook with edge case
140	  data.
141	
142	**Negative / risks**
143	
144	- Figma cannot be read automatically here, so token mapping needs manual
145	  verification against the designs.
146	- Breakpoint values are duplicated as literals in CSS and can drift from
147	  `design-system.css`.
148	- The rate-selection rule is an assumption until confirmed with the designs.
149	
150	## Acceptance criteria
151	
152	The task is successful when all of the following hold:
153	
154	- [ ] **Car Block** component matches the design.
155	- [ ] **Car List** component renders the full set of cars from the fixture.
156	- [ ] Both are **responsive** (mobile → tablet → desktop).
157	- [ ] Styling uses the **design system** tokens and classes from
158	      `design-system.css`, with no ad-hoc values.
159	- [ ] **Storybook stories** exist for each component (happy path and
160	      interesting edge cases).
161	- [ ] **Unit tests** (Vitest + Testing Library) are colocated with each
162	      component.
163	- [ ] **`AGENTS.md`** with instructions for AI agents is present at the repo
164	      root and committed.
165	- [ ] `npm run lint` passes cleanly.
166	- [ ] `npm test` passes cleanly.
167	- [ ] `npm run build` passes.
168	
169	Stretch goals ("Impress us"): accessibility (semantic HTML, keyboard
170	navigation, ARIA, focus states), loading, empty and error states in stories,
171	small composable sub-components, lazy images, and a well organized Storybook.

**Guidelines.** The file map and conventions in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` now say:
- **Feature folders:** each feature is a folder, `src/components/<Feature>/`. It holds the component and everything only that feature needs: CSS, tests, stories, helpers and an `index.ts`.
- **Sub-features:** they sit directly under their parent, such as `CarBlock/Badge/`, with no intermediate `components/` folder. Nesting follows the same rules at every level.
- **Naming and stories:** files match their folder name, like `Badge/Badge.tsx`. Only top-level features get stories.
- **Imports:** use `@/` outside a feature. Inside a feature, use relative imports only for siblings and descendants, never `../`. Other features are imported through their `index.ts`.
- **Shared code:** anything used by two or more features moves up to the lowest common parent. A dependency used only by sibling sub-features, such as the icons, becomes its own sub-feature folder.

**Target layout**
```
src/components/
  CarList/    CarList.tsx .css .test.tsx .stories.tsx, index.ts
  CarBlock/   CarBlock.tsx .css .test.tsx .stories.tsx, index.ts,
              money.ts, carRental.ts (each with its test)
    Badge/ Features/ Location/ Media/ Price/ Vendor/   (X.tsx, X.test.tsx, index.ts)
    Icons/    (was components/icons/CarIcons)

The card title now follows the four sizes you gave. `lint`, `build` and the 62 tests pass, and I haven't looked at it in the browser.

| Card | Figma style | How it's set |
|---|---|---|
| Small | Body-L | the class `ts-body-l-heavy` (1rem, line height 1.5) |
| Medium (400px and up) | Subtitle-S | `font-size: calc(var(--space-200) + var(--space-050) / 2)` = 1.125rem, `line-height: calc(var(--space-300) + var(--space-050))` = 1.75rem |
| Large and XL (700px and up) | Subtitle-M | `--space-250` for the size and `--space-400` for the line height, as before |

Weight stays 700 at every size, because the base class is the heavy one.

**Medium uses a `calc()` instead of one variable.** No single variable equals 1.125rem. The nearest are `--space-200` (1rem) and `--space-250` (1.25rem), and either would make Medium look like Small or Large. So I combined two spacing variables, which gives the exact size. This is the same approach the file already uses for the Medium image height.

**The Medium line height is slightly off.** Subtitle-S's 1.55 line height works out to about 1.74rem, and the closest I can build is 1.75rem, about 0.1px more.

The title's typography notes in `NOTES.md` are rewritten with a table of the three sizes and what each is built from. The title row and assumption A27 in the spec now say the same. Spec A27 still says the other text doesn't change per size, so tell me if the price or the feature rows do.

Base directory for this skill: /home/rhoger-anacleto/react-assessment-main/.claude/skills/commit

# commit

Commit the current work with a message that passes `@commitlint/config-conventional`. Invoking this skill is the user's request to commit; it does **not** authorize pushing, amending, or rewriting history.

## Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

- **type** (required, lowercase): `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`.
- **scope** (optional, lowercase, kebab-case): the area changed. Suggested for this repo: `car-block`, `car-list`, `types`, `design-system`, `storybook`, `adr`, `docs`, `plans`, `agents`, `skills`, `config`, `deps`. Reuse the scopes in `git log` when they fit; omit the scope when the change spans areas.
- **subject** (required): imperative mood ("add", not "added"), lowercase first letter, no trailing period, header (whole first line) ≤ 100 characters. Describe _what_ and _why it matters_, not the file list.
- **body** (optional): blank line before it, wrapped at 100 characters. Explain motivation and non-obvious decisions.
- **footer** (optional): blank line before it. Breaking changes: `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` (or `!` after type/scope: `feat(car-list)!: …`). References: `Refs: #123`. Trailers such as `Co-Authored-By:` go here.

Type guide: `feat` new behaviour/component · `fix` bug fix · `docs` ADRs, plans, README, CLAUDE/AGENTS · `test` tests only · `refactor` no behaviour change · `style` formatting only (not CSS styling work, which is `feat`/`fix`) · `build` deps/bundler/tsconfig · `ci` pipelines · `chore` anything else non-source (agent/skill files are `chore(agents)` / `chore(skills)`, or `docs` if purely documentation) · `perf` · `revert`.

## Workflow

1. **Check the repo.** Run `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`. If this is not a git repository, tell the user and ask whether to `git init`; don't initialise on your own.
2. **Inspect.** Run `git status --short`, `git diff` and `git diff --staged`, and `git log --oneline -10` to match existing scopes and style. If nothing changed, say so and stop.
3. **Group the changes.** One commit = one logical change. If the diff mixes unrelated work (e.g. a component and an unrelated docs edit), split it into several commits, each staged separately. Propose the split if it isn't obvious.
4. **Check what you are about to commit.**
   - Never stage `.env*` (except `.env.example`), tokens, credentials, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `storybook-static/`, `coverage/`, or generated junk. If a secret appears in the diff, stop and warn the user.
   - Stage explicit paths (`git add <paths>`), never `git add -A` / `git add .`, unless the user asked to commit everything and you reviewed the full list.
   - If code changed, run `npm run lint` and `npm test` first when they are quick, and mention failures; don't commit known-broken code without the user's say-so. Docs-only commits don't need them.
5. **Write the message** following the format above, based on the staged diff (not on the conversation alone). Prefer a body when the _why_ isn't obvious from the subject.
6. **Validate** with commitlint (config: `commitlint.config.js`, extends `@commitlint/config-conventional`) before committing:
   ```bash
   printf '%s\n' "<full message>" | npx --no -- commitlint
   ```
   Fix any reported problem and re-run until it passes. The husky `commit-msg` hook (`.husky/commit-msg`) runs the same check on `git commit`, so a message that fails here will be rejected there. If `@commitlint/cli` isn't installed (`npx --no -- commitlint --version` fails), tell the user to run `npm install` (or install per "Setup" below); in the meantime follow the format above by hand and say that it was not machine-validated.
7. **Commit.** Use a heredoc so multi-line messages keep their formatting:
   ```bash
   git commit -F - <<'EOF'
   feat(car-block): render vehicle details and price

   Body explaining why, wrapped at 100 characters.

   Co-Authored-By: …
   EOF
   ```
   Append the attribution trailer the session instructs (the system/CLAUDE.md attribution line for commits) as the last footer line, after a blank line. Never invent one.
8. **Report** the resulting hash(es) and subjects (`git log --oneline -n <count>`), and anything left uncommitted.

## Setup (one-time, needs the user)

The repo is wired for [commitlint](https://github.com/conventional-changelog/commitlint) + [husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/): `commitlint.config.js` and `.husky/commit-msg` exist, but the packages must be installed and the repo must be a git repository for the hook to activate:

```bash
npm install -D @commitlint/cli @commitlint/config-conventional husky
npm pkg set scripts.prepare="husky"
npm run prepare   # points git at .husky (needs `git init` first)
```

Adding dependencies and the `prepare` script changes `package.json`; do it only with the user's go-ahead, and never work around registry authentication errors yourself.

## Rules

- Never use `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `--amend`, `git reset --hard`, or force-push unless the user explicitly asks. If a hook fails, fix the cause and make a **new** commit.
- Never push, tag, or open a PR as part of this skill; offer it afterwards.
- Don't change git config.
- If commitlint or the hook rejects the message, don't bypass it; fix the message.
- Keep subjects specific: `feat(car-list): render one block per car` beats `feat: update components`.

## Examples

```
feat(car-block): add vehicle details and price summary
fix(car-list): keep list semantic when the response is empty
test(car-block): cover formatted price and cancellation policy
docs(adr): record car block and car list decision
chore(skills): add figma-spec extraction skill
build(deps): add @vitest/coverage-v8
refactor(types): split rental rate types from vehicle types
feat(car-block)!: require a Car prop instead of raw JSON

BREAKING CHANGE: CarBlock no longer accepts the response envelope.
```

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in this repo.

## Project overview

React assessment starter (CarTrawler-style car rental UI). The task (see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`) is to build two **responsive** Storybook components that match the Figma designs:

1. **Car Block** — a single car result card (vehicle details, pricing, policies).
2. **Car List** — a list of Car Blocks rendered from every car in `src/assets/response.json`.

Reviewers weigh _how_ the code is built (clean structure, design-system fidelity, tests, a11y) as much as the result. Prefer small, composable, well-typed components.

The deliverable also requires an `AGENTS.md` at the repo root (instructions for AI agents). Keep it in sync with this file.

## Stack

Vite 8, React 19, TypeScript 5.9 (strict), Storybook 10 (`@storybook/react-vite`), Vitest 5 + Testing Library (jsdom), ESLint 10 flat config + Prettier. Node 24 (`.nvmrc`).

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run dev            # Vite dev server  :5173
npm run storybook      # Storybook        :6006
npm test               # Vitest, single run
npm run test:watch     # Vitest watch
npm run lint           # ESLint (lint:fix to auto-fix)
npm run format         # Prettier write (format:check to verify)
npm run build          # tsc -b && vite build (type-check + bundle)
npm run build-storybook
```

## File map

```
src/
  assets/response.json     # fixture: { productType, searchId, responseTime, cars[], vendors[], locations[] }
  types/carRental.ts       # types shared by several features, modelled on response.json (no runtime code)
  data/searchResponse.ts   # the fixture typed as SearchResponse (components never import the JSON)
  components/              # one folder per feature; CarBlock/ is the pattern to follow
    CarList/               # CarList.tsx/.css/.test.tsx/.stories.tsx + index.ts
    CarBlock/              # CarBlock.tsx/.css/.test.tsx/.stories.tsx + index.ts
      money.ts             # formatMoney / divideMoney / isZeroMoney (only place that parses Money.amount); tests next to it
      carRental.ts         # selectRate + formatters for the card; tests next to it
      Badge/ Features/ Location/ Media/ Price/ Vendor/   # sub-features, each X.tsx + X.test.tsx + index.ts (no stories)
      Icons/               # inline SVG icons used by Features and Media (no icon dependency)
  design-system.css        # tokens + typography utility classes (source of truth for styling)
  App.tsx, App.css, main.tsx
docs/
  adr/                     # architecture decision records (0001 = Car Block / Car List)
  design/<slug>/           # design specs (spec.md, ...); car-block-and-car-list/spec.md is manual, derived from the PNGs in docs/design/ because Figma was not exportable
  plans/                   # development plans written by the architect agent
.claude/skills/figma-spec/ # skill that turns a Figma link into docs/design/<slug>/
.claude/skills/commit/     # skill that commits with the commitlint conventional format
.claude/agents/            # agent definitions (architect, implementer, qa-specialist)
.storybook/                # main.ts (stories glob), preview.ts (imports design-system.css)
vite.config.ts             # Vite + Vitest config, `@` alias
vitest.setup.ts            # jest-dom matchers
commitlint.config.js       # commitlint rules (extends config-conventional)
.husky/commit-msg          # git hook that runs commitlint on every commit
```

## Workflow

1. **Architect** (`.claude/agents/architect.md`) reads the ADR, obtains the Figma spec and writes a detailed development plan to `docs/plans/<slug>.md`.
2. **Human approval gate.** The plan is written as `Status: DRAFT — awaiting human approval`. A human must review it and explicitly approve it or request changes; changes bump `Revision` and keep it DRAFT. Only an explicit approval sets `Status: APPROVED by <name> on <date> (revision <n>)`. Agents never approve a plan themselves; when the architect returns, ask the user to approve or request changes before implementing.
3. **Implementer** (`.claude/agents/implementer.md`) starts only when the plan header reads `APPROVED`, then follows it step by step, building from the local spec and never calling Figma. If the plan changes after approval it returns to DRAFT.
4. **QA specialist** (`.claude/agents/qa-specialist.md`) audits the code against the plan and ADR acceptance criteria, writes success-path tests to reach at least 80% coverage, then starts Storybook and the dev server so a human can compare the result with Figma.
5. **Final human acceptance.** QA leaves `QA Status: AWAITING HUMAN APPROVAL` in the plan. Only the human's explicit approval sets `QA Status: ACCEPTED by <name> on <date>`; reported design differences go back to the implementer as a defect list. The feature is done only when ACCEPTED.
6. Verify against the definition of done below.

There is no user-story step; the ADR acceptance criteria are the requirements.

### Agents (`.claude/agents/`)

| Agent         | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | May edit                                 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| architect     | Reads the ADR, gets the Figma spec via the `figma-spec` skill, writes the detailed plan as a DRAFT and stops at the approval gate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `docs/plans/` only                       |
| implementer   | Reads an APPROVED plan and builds it with the project standards: tokens-only CSS, colocated component/test/stories, strict TS. Refuses to start on a non-APPROVED plan, never calls Figma, runs lint/test/build/format:check before reporting.                                                                                                                              | `src/` and the plan's checkboxes         |
| qa-specialist | Feature-agnostic: audits the code against any approved plan and its ADR criteria, writes success-path tests for at least 80% coverage of the changed code (coverage needs `@vitest/coverage-v8`; ask before adding it), runs the app for the human to review (against the design spec when there is one), and waits for final human approval. Never fixes application code. | `*.test.ts(x)` and the plan's QA section |

The implementer stops and reports (instead of deviating) if the plan is wrong or ambiguous; scope or design changes send the plan back to DRAFT for re-approval. Visual fidelity still needs a human check in Storybook.

## Architecture & conventions

- **Imports**: use the `@/` alias for anything under `src/` (`import CarList from "@/components/CarList"`). Relative imports only inside one feature folder: siblings and descendants (`./Badge`, `./money`), never `../`. Cross-feature imports go through the other feature's `index.ts`, not its internals.
- **Feature folders**: each feature is a folder `src/components/<Feature>/` holding the component and everything only it needs: `.css`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.stories.tsx`, helpers, and an `index.ts` re-exporting the component (named and default). A feature made of several parts nests them directly under it as sub-feature folders (`CarBlock/Badge/`), with no intermediate `components/` folder, and recurses with the same rules. File names match their folder (`Badge/Badge.tsx`). Stories for top-level features; sub-features get tests, plus a story only when comparing their variants visually helps (title `Components/<Feature>/<Sub>`, e.g. `CarBlock/Badge`). Anything used by two or more features moves up to the lowest common parent (types and fixture data shared app-wide stay in `src/types/` and `src/data/`). A dependency used only by sibling sub-features (e.g. `Icons/`) is its own sub-feature folder under their parent.
- **Styling files**: one `.css` per feature folder, imported by the feature's root component; sub-features may use the parent's classes (BEM-style `car-block__badge`) or add their own `.css` if they grow. Components are exported both named and default (see `CarBlock.tsx`).
- **Props**: declare a `type XProps` above the component with JSDoc on each prop; Storybook `argTypes` mirror them.
- **Styling**: plain CSS files imported by the component (no CSS-in-JS/Tailwind). Style **only** with design-system tokens — never hard-code colors, px spacing, radii or font sizes if a token exists:
  - Colors: `--text-*`, `--bg-fill-*`, `--border-*`, `--button-*`, `--price-*`, `--surface-*`, `--container-*`, etc.
  - Typography: apply `.ts-display-*`, `.ts-headline-*`, `.ts-subtitle-*`, `.ts-body-*`, `.ts-label-*`, `.ts-button-*` classes.
  - Spacing/sizing: `--space-*`, `--bw-*` (border width), `--br-*` (radius).
  - Breakpoints: mobile 608px, tablet 840px, desktop-small 1025px, desktop-large 1328px. CSS custom properties can't be used inside `@media` conditions, so write the literal px value and note which breakpoint it mirrors in a comment. Design mobile-first (`min-width`).
  - Read exact tokens off Figma; don't guess. Figma: see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
  - **Don't call Figma while building.** Use the `figma-spec` skill (`.claude/skills/figma-spec/`) to extract a Figma link once into `docs/design/<slug>/spec.md` (token-mapped colors, spacing, radii, typography, layout), then build from that file. Reuse an existing spec instead of re-fetching; only refresh if the design changed. Needs `FIGMA_TOKEN` in a git-ignored `.env`; never print or commit it.
- **Types**: model them on `response.json` (`vehicle`, `rentalRates[]` with `pricing`, `deposit`, `fuelPolicy`, `mileagePolicy`, `insuranceCoverage`, `config`). Money values are `{ amount: string, currency: string }` — amounts are strings; format via `Intl.NumberFormat`, don't parse ad hoc. Put shared types in a dedicated types file under `src/`, not inside components. Do not use `any`.
- **TypeScript rules in force**: `strict`, `noUnusedLocals/Parameters`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type` for types), `erasableSyntaxOnly` (no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties).
- **ESLint**: `react-hooks` rules and `react-refresh/only-export-components` (warn) — keep non-component exports out of component files.
- **Formatting** (Prettier): double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 80 cols, 2-space indent. Run `npm run format` rather than hand-formatting.
- **Commits**: Conventional Commits enforced by commitlint (`@commitlint/config-conventional`) through a husky `commit-msg` hook: `type(scope): subject`, lowercase imperative subject, no trailing period, header ≤ 100 chars. Use the `commit` skill (`.claude/skills/commit/`) to stage explicit files, validate and commit; never `--no-verify`, never amend/push unless asked. Packages are installed per the skill's Setup section (needs `git init` and `npm install`).
- **Accessibility**: semantic HTML (lists for the Car List, headings in a sensible order), meaningful `alt` text on car images, visible focus states, keyboard-operable controls.
- **Performance**: `loading="lazy"` on images; memoize only where it measurably matters.

## Testing

- Vitest globals are on, but the existing tests still import `describe/it/expect` from `vitest` — follow that.
- Query by role/text (`getByRole`, `getByText`) first; `data-testid` only as a fallback.
- Use `userEvent.setup()` for interactions.
- Test with the real fixture (or a slice of it) for Car Block / Car List: renders every car, key fields (make/model, price, policies), edge cases (missing optional fields, empty list).

## Storybook

- Title convention: `Components/<Name>`, with `tags: ["autodocs"]` and typed `Meta`/`StoryObj`.
- Cover the happy path plus edge cases: long names, missing image, no insurance, free cancellation vs. fee, empty list, loading/error states for the list.
- Verify responsive behavior with Storybook viewports (mobile/tablet/desktop).

## Definition of done

- Matches Figma at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
- Uses design-system tokens/classes only.
- Stories and colocated unit tests exist for each component.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass cleanly.
- `AGENTS.md` is present and up to date.

## Boundaries — ask before changing

- `src/design-system.css` (read-only source of truth; add local CSS in component files instead).
- `src/assets/response.json` (fixture; build edge cases as story/test data derived from it).
- Tooling config: `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.json`, `commitlint.config.js`, `.husky/*`, `.storybook/*`, `package.json` dependencies.
- Don't add new dependencies without asking. Never commit `node_modules`, `dist` or `storybook-static`.

86	- **Feature folders**: each feature is a folder `src/components/<Feature>/` holding the component and everything only it needs: `.css`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.stories.tsx`, helpers, and an `index.ts` re-exporting the component (named and default). A feature made of several parts nests them directly under it as sub-feature folders (`CarBlock/Badge/`), with no intermediate `components/` folder, and recurses with the same rules. File names match their folder (`Badge/Badge.tsx`). Stories for top-level features; sub-features get tests, plus a story only when comparing their variants visually helps (title `Components/<Feature>/<Sub>`, e.g. `CarBlock/Badge`). Anything used by two or more features moves up to the lowest common parent (types and fixture data shared app-wide stay in `src/types/` and `src/data/`). A dependency used only by sibling sub-features (e.g. `Icons/`) is its own sub-feature folder under their parent.
87	- **Styling files**: one `.css` per feature folder, imported by the feature's root component; sub-features may use the parent's classes (BEM-style `car-block__badge`) or add their own `.css` if they grow. Components are exported both named and default (see `CarBlock.tsx`).
88	- **Props**: declare a `type XProps` above the component with JSDoc on each prop; Storybook `argTypes` mirror them.
89	- **Styling**: plain CSS files imported by the component (no CSS-in-JS/Tailwind). Style **only** with design-system tokens — never hard-code colors, px spacing, radii or font sizes if a token exists:
90	  - Colors: `--text-*`, `--bg-fill-*`, `--border-*`, `--button-*`, `--price-*`, `--surface-*`, `--container-*`, etc.
91	  - Typography: apply `.ts-display-*`, `.ts-headline-*`, `.ts-subtitle-*`, `.ts-body-*`, `.ts-label-*`, `.ts-button-*` classes.
92	  - Spacing/sizing: `--space-*`, `--bw-*` (border width), `--br-*` (radius).
93	  - Breakpoints: mobile 608px, tablet 840px, desktop-small 1025px, desktop-large 1328px. CSS custom properties can't be used inside `@media` conditions, so write the literal px value and note which breakpoint it mirrors in a comment. Design mobile-first (`min-width`).
94	  - Read exact tokens off Figma; don't guess. Figma: see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
95	  - **Don't call Figma while building.** Use the `figma-spec` skill (`.claude/skills/figma-spec/`) to extract a Figma link once into `docs/design/<slug>/spec.md` (token-mapped colors, spacing, radii, typography, layout), then build from that file. Reuse an existing spec instead of re-fetching; only refresh if the design changed. Needs `FIGMA_TOKEN` in a git-ignored `.env`; never print or commit it.
96	- **Types**: model them on `response.json` (`vehicle`, `rentalRates[]` with `pricing`, `deposit`, `fuelPolicy`, `mileagePolicy`, `insuranceCoverage`, `config`). Money values are `{ amount: string, currency: string }` — amounts are strings; format via `Intl.NumberFormat`, don't parse ad hoc. Put shared types in a dedicated types file under `src/`, not inside components. Do not use `any`.
97	- **TypeScript rules in force**: `strict`, `noUnusedLocals/Parameters`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type` for types), `erasableSyntaxOnly` (no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties).
98	- **ESLint**: `react-hooks` rules and `react-refresh/only-export-components` (warn) — keep non-component exports out of component files.
99	- **Formatting** (Prettier): double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 80 cols, 2-space indent. Run `npm run format` rather than hand-formatting.
100	- **Commits**: Conventional Commits enforced by commitlint (`@commitlint/config-conventional`) through a husky `commit-msg` hook: `type(scope): subject`, lowercase imperative subject, no trailing period, header ≤ 100 chars. Use the `commit` skill (`.claude/skills/commit/`) to stage explicit files, validate and commit; never `--no-verify`, never amend/push unless asked. Packages are installed per the skill's Setup section (needs `git init` and `npm install`).
101	- **Accessibility**: semantic HTML (lists for the Car List, headings in a sensible order), meaningful `alt` text on car images, visible focus states, keyboard-operable controls.
102	- **Performance**: `loading="lazy"` on images; memoize only where it measurably matters.
103	
104	## Testing
105	
106	- Vitest globals are on, but the existing tests still import `describe/it/expect` from `vitest` — follow that.
107	- Query by role/text (`getByRole`, `getByText`) first; `data-testid` only as a fallback.
108	- Use `userEvent.setup()` for interactions.
109	- Test with the real fixture (or a slice of it) for Car Block / Car List: renders every car, key fields (make/model, price, policies), edge cases (missing optional fields, empty list).
110	
111	## Storybook
112	
113	- Title convention: `Components/<Name>`, with `tags: ["autodocs"]` and typed `Meta`/`StoryObj`.
114	- Cover the happy path plus edge cases: long names, missing image, no insurance, free cancellation vs. fee, empty list, loading/error states for the list.
115	- Verify responsive behavior with Storybook viewports (mobile/tablet/desktop).
116	
117	## Definition of done
118	
119	- Matches Figma at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
120	- Uses design-system tokens/classes only.
121	- Stories and colocated unit tests exist for each component.
122	- `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass cleanly.
123	- `AGENTS.md` is present and up to date.
124	
125	## Boundaries — ask before changing
126	
127	- `src/design-system.css` (read-only source of truth; add local CSS in component files instead).
128	- `src/assets/response.json` (fixture; build edge cases as story/test data derived from it).
129	- Tooling config: `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.json`, `commitlint.config.js`, `.husky/*`, `.storybook/*`, `package.json` dependencies.
130	- Don't add new dependencies without asking. Never commit `node_modules`, `dist` or `storybook-static`.
131

Result of calling the Read tool:
1	# ADR 0001: Car Block and Car List components
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-10-21
5	- **Deciders:** rhoger.anacleto
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	### Task description
10	
11	Build two React components that render car rental search results, documented
12	in Storybook and covered by unit tests (see `INSTRUCTIONS.md`):
13	
14	1. **Car Block** — a single car result card showing vehicle details, pricing
15	   and policies for one car.
16	2. **Car List** — a list of Car Blocks, one for every car in
17	   `src/assets/response.json`.
18	
19	Design source:
20	[CarTrawler Technical Assessment — Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/JlbW0v2Tmf6kybsOEFyhGx/CarTrawler-Technical-Assesment?node-id=10308-24250&t=JXUySO69t2VzVSnO-0)
21	(also linked in `INSTRUCTIONS.md`).
22	
23	Constraints:
24	
25	- Both components must be **responsive** across mobile, tablet and desktop.
26	- Figma is the source of truth for layout, spacing and styling.
27	- All styling must come from the design system in `src/design-system.css`
28	  (CSS variables and `.ts-*` utility classes), not ad-hoc values.
29	- Types are modelled on the fixture: each car has a `vehicle` and
30	  `rentalRates[]` (pricing, deposit, cancellation, fuel and mileage policy,
31	  insurance coverage, config flags).
32	- Stack is fixed: React 19, strict TypeScript, Vite, Storybook 10, Vitest +
33	  Testing Library, ESLint + Prettier. Components, tests and stories are
34	  colocated and imported through the `@/` alias.
35	- An `AGENTS.md` for AI agents working in the repo is also required. AI
36	  assistance is encouraged.
37	
38	## Alternatives considered
39	
40	### 1. Styling
41	
42	| Option                                             | Pros                                                                             | Cons                                                                        |
43	| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
44	| **Plain colocated CSS using design-system tokens** | Matches the `Counter` pattern; tokens and `.ts-*` classes used directly; no deps | Class naming discipline is manual                                           |
45	| CSS Modules                                        | Scoped class names                                                               | Extra convention not used by the starter; stories and tests need no benefit |
46	| Tailwind or CSS-in-JS                              | Fast to write                                                                    | New dependency; duplicates the existing design system; against the brief    |
47	| Inline styles                                      | No stylesheet                                                                    | No media queries or pseudo-states; encourages hard-coded values             |
48	
49	### 2. Component structure
50	
51	| Option                                                         | Pros                                                         | Cons                               |
52	| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
53	| One monolithic `CarBlock`                                      | Fewest files                                                 | Hard to test, read and reuse       |
54	| **`CarBlock` composed of small presentational sub-components** | Each piece is testable and readable; clean, well-typed props | More files; needs a sensible split |
55	
56	### 3. Data and types
57	
58	| Option                                                | Pros                                                | Cons                                     |
59	| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
60	| Import `response.json` and let TypeScript infer types | Zero effort                                         | Literal-inferred types; fragile; no docs |
61	| **Dedicated types file modelled on `response.json`**  | Explicit, reusable by components, tests and stories | Must be kept in sync with the fixture    |
62	
63	`CarBlock` receives a single `Car`; `CarList` receives `Car[]`. Components do
64	not import the JSON themselves, so they stay reusable and easy to feed edge
65	case data.
66	
67	### 4. Responsiveness
68	
69	| Option                                     | Pros                                                     | Cons                                                              |
70	| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| **Mobile-first `min-width` media queries** | Simple, universal, matches the design-system breakpoints | `var(--breakpoint-*)` cannot be used in `@media`; literals needed |
72	| Container queries                          | Component adapts to its container                        | Breakpoints in the design system are viewport-based               |
73	| JS-based breakpoints (`matchMedia` hooks)  | Conditional rendering possible                           | Extra runtime logic, flicker, harder to test                      |
74	
75	### 5. Testing
76	
77	| Option                                                   | Pros                                 | Cons                             |
78	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
79	| **Testing Library by role and text, using fixture data** | Tests behaviour users see; resilient | Slightly more verbose            |
80	| Snapshot tests                                           | Quick to write                       | Brittle, low signal, noisy diffs |
81	
82	### 6. Cars with several `rentalRates`
83	
84	| Option                                               | Pros                                  | Cons                                         |
85	| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
86	| **Render one rate: the one with the best relevance** | Matches a "single result card" design | Must confirm the rule against Figma and data |
87	| Render all rates in the block                        | Shows everything                      | Not what the design shows; clutters the card |
88	
89	## Decision
90	
91	Build `CarBlock` and `CarList` as small, typed, presentational React
92	components styled with plain colocated CSS that uses only design-system
93	tokens, designed mobile-first.
94	
95	### How
96	
97	- **Layout of files** under `src/components/`, following `Counter`:
98	  `CarBlock.tsx`, `CarBlock.css`, `CarBlock.test.tsx`, `CarBlock.stories.tsx`,
99	  and the same four files for `CarList`. Small sub-components (for example
100	  vehicle info, price, policies) live next to `CarBlock` and are composed by
101	  it.
102	- **Types** live in a dedicated types file under `src/`, modelled on
103	  `response.json`. Money values are `{ amount: string; currency: string }`
104	  and are formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`, never parsed ad hoc.
105	- **Styling** uses `var(--token)` and `.ts-*` classes only. Each visual
106	  property is mapped to its token by inspecting Figma. Media queries are
107	  `min-width` with literal px values mirroring `--breakpoint-mobile` (608px),
108	  `--breakpoint-tablet` (840px), `--breakpoint-desktop-small` (1025px) and
109	  `--breakpoint-desktop-large` (1328px), each with a comment naming the token.
110	- **Semantics and accessibility:** `CarList` renders a `<ul>` of `<li>`;
111	  `CarBlock` is an `<article>` with a heading; images have meaningful `alt`
112	  text and `loading="lazy"`; interactive elements are keyboard-operable with
113	  visible focus.
114	- **Rate selection:** show the rental rate with the lowest `orderByRelevance`
115	  (to be confirmed against Figma); cars without rates render a safe fallback
116	  rather than crashing.
117	- **Stories** use title `Components/<Name>` with `autodocs`. They cover the
118	  happy path and edge cases (long names, missing image, no insurance, free
119	  cancellation vs fee, empty list, loading and error states for the list).
120	- **Tests** query by role and text and use the real fixture (or slices of it).
121	  They check that the list renders every car, key fields of a block, and the
122	  edge cases above.
123	
124	### Why
125	
126	- Design-system tokens keep the result consistent with the brand and are an
127	  explicit requirement; hard-coded values would fail review.
128	- Plain CSS adds no dependency and follows the existing starter pattern.
129	- Small composed components keep each unit readable and testable, and show
130	  structural judgment, which the assessment evaluates.
131	- Typing from the fixture makes the data contract explicit and gives
132	  compile-time safety for stories and tests.
133	- Mobile-first media queries are the simplest approach that satisfies the
134	  design-system breakpoints without runtime logic.
135	- Behavioural tests survive refactors; snapshots would not.
136	
137	## Consequences
138	
139	**Positive**
140	
141	- No new dependencies; consistent with `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`
142	  conventions.
143	- Components are reusable and easy to exercise from Storybook with edge case
144	  data.
145	
146	**Negative / risks**
147	
148	- Figma cannot be read automatically here, so token mapping needs manual
149	  verification against the designs.
150	- Breakpoint values are duplicated as literals in CSS and can drift from
151	  `design-system.css`.
152	- The rate-selection rule is an assumption until confirmed with the designs.
153	
154	## Acceptance criteria
155	
156	The task is successful when all of the following hold:
157	
158	- [ ] **Car Block** component matches the design.
159	- [ ] **Car List** component renders the full set of cars from the fixture.
160	- [ ] Both are **responsive** (mobile → tablet → desktop).
161	- [ ] Styling uses the **design system** tokens and classes from
162	      `design-system.css`, with no ad-hoc values.
163	- [ ] **Storybook stories** exist for each component (happy path and
164	      interesting edge cases).
165	- [ ] **Unit tests** (Vitest + Testing Library) are colocated with each
166	      component.
167	- [ ] **`AGENTS.md`** with instructions for AI agents is present at the repo
168	      root and committed.
169	- [ ] `npm run lint` passes cleanly.
170	- [ ] `npm test` passes cleanly.
171	- [ ] `npm run build` passes.
172	
173	Stretch goals ("Impress us"): accessibility (semantic HTML, keyboard
174	navigation, ARIA, focus states), loading, empty and error states in stories,
175	small composable sub-components, lazy images, and a well organized Storybook.
176

# commit

Commit the current work with a message that passes `@commitlint/config-conventional`. Invoking this skill is the user's request to commit; it does **not** authorize pushing, amending, or rewriting history.

## Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

- **type** (required, lowercase): `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`.
- **scope** (optional, lowercase, kebab-case): the area changed. Suggested for this repo: `car-block`, `car-list`, `types`, `design-system`, `storybook`, `adr`, `docs`, `plans`, `agents`, `skills`, `config`, `deps`. Reuse the scopes in `git log` when they fit; omit the scope when the change spans areas.
- **subject** (required): imperative mood ("add", not "added"), lowercase first letter, no trailing period, header (whole first line) ≤ 100 characters. Describe _what_ and _why it matters_, not the file list.
- **body** (optional): blank line before it, wrapped at 100 characters. Explain motivation and non-obvious decisions.
- **footer** (optional): blank line before it. Breaking changes: `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` (or `!` after type/scope: `feat(car-list)!: …`). References: `Refs: #123`. Trailers such as `Co-Authored-By:` go here.

Type guide: `feat` new behaviour/component · `fix` bug fix · `docs` ADRs, plans, README, CLAUDE/AGENTS · `test` tests only · `refactor` no behaviour change · `style` formatting only (not CSS styling work, which is `feat`/`fix`) · `build` deps/bundler/tsconfig · `ci` pipelines · `chore` anything else non-source (agent/skill files are `chore(agents)` / `chore(skills)`, or `docs` if purely documentation) · `perf` · `revert`.

## Workflow

1. **Check the repo.** Run `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`. If this is not a git repository, tell the user and ask whether to `git init`; don't initialise on your own.
2. **Inspect.** Run `git status --short`, `git diff` and `git diff --staged`, and `git log --oneline -10` to match existing scopes and style. If nothing changed, say so and stop.
3. **Group the changes.** One commit = one logical change. If the diff mixes unrelated work (e.g. a component and an unrelated docs edit), split it into several commits, each staged separately. Propose the split if it isn't obvious.
4. **Check what you are about to commit.**
   - Never stage `.env*` (except `.env.example`), tokens, credentials, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `storybook-static/`, `coverage/`, or generated junk. If a secret appears in the diff, stop and warn the user.
   - Stage explicit paths (`git add <paths>`), never `git add -A` / `git add .`, unless the user asked to commit everything and you reviewed the full list.
   - If code changed, run `npm run lint` and `npm test` first when they are quick, and mention failures; don't commit known-broken code without the user's say-so. Docs-only commits don't need them.
5. **Write the message** following the format above, based on the staged diff (not on the conversation alone). Prefer a body when the _why_ isn't obvious from the subject.
6. **Validate** with commitlint (config: `commitlint.config.js`, extends `@commitlint/config-conventional`) before committing:
   ```bash
   printf '%s\n' "<full message>" | npx --no -- commitlint
   ```
   Fix any reported problem and re-run until it passes. The husky `commit-msg` hook (`.husky/commit-msg`) runs the same check on `git commit`, so a message that fails here will be rejected there. If `@commitlint/cli` isn't installed (`npx --no -- commitlint --version` fails), tell the user to run `npm install` (or install per "Setup" below); in the meantime follow the format above by hand and say that it was not machine-validated.
7. **Commit.** Use a heredoc so multi-line messages keep their formatting:
   ```bash
   git commit -F - <<'EOF'
   feat(car-block): render vehicle details and price

   Body explaining why, wrapped at 100 characters.

   Co-Authored-By: …
   EOF
   ```
   Append the attribution trailer the session instructs (the system/CLAUDE.md attribution line for commits) as the last footer line, after a blank line. Never invent one.
8. **Report** the resulting hash(es) and subjects (`git log --oneline -n <count>`), and anything left uncommitted.

## Setup (one-time, needs the user)

The repo is wired for [commitlint](https://github.com/conventional-changelog/commitlint) + [husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/): `commitlint.config.js` and `.husky/commit-msg` exist, but the packages must be installed and the repo must be a git repository for the hook to activate:

```bash
npm install -D @commitlint/cli @commitlint/config-conventional husky
npm pkg set scripts.prepare="husky"
npm run prepare   # points git at .husky (needs `git init` first)
```

Adding dependencies and the `prepare` script changes `package.json`; do it only with the user's go-ahead, and never work around registry authentication errors yourself.

## Rules

- Never use `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `--amend`, `git reset --hard`, or force-push unless the user explicitly asks. If a hook fails, fix the cause and make a **new** commit.
- Never push, tag, or open a PR as part of this skill; offer it afterwards.
- Don't change git config.
- If commitlint or the hook rejects the message, don't bypass it; fix the message.
- Keep subjects specific: `feat(car-list): render one block per car` beats `feat: update components`.

## Examples

```
feat(car-block): add vehicle details and price summary
fix(car-list): keep list semantic when the response is empty
test(car-block): cover formatted price and cancellation policy
docs(adr): record car block and car list decision
chore(skills): add figma-spec extraction skill
build(deps): add @vitest/coverage-v8
refactor(types): split rental rate types from vehicle types
feat(car-block)!: require a Car prop instead of raw JSON

BREAKING CHANGE: CarBlock no longer accepts the response envelope.
```

Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- architect: Architect for this repo. Reads the ADR, gets the Figma design as a local spec (via the figma-spec skill), and writes a detailed, step-by-step development plan in docs/plans/ for the implementer agent. Use before building or changing any component. Plans only; never writes application code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Skill)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- implementer: Implements an APPROVED development plan from docs/plans/ following this repo's standards (design-system tokens, colocated component/test/stories, strict TypeScript). Use only after the architect's plan has been approved by a human. Builds from the local Figma spec and never calls Figma. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- qa-specialist: QA for this repo, independent of any particular feature. Takes an approved plan and its ADR, audits the implemented code against the plan and the ADR acceptance criteria, writes success-path tests to reach at least 80% coverage of the changed code, starts the app so a human can review it (against the design spec when the plan has one), and stops at a final human acceptance gate. Use after the implementer reports done. Writes tests only; never changes application code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- commit: Create git commits that follow the commitlint conventional format (type(scope): subject, with optional body and footer), staging only the intended files and validating the message before committing. Use when the user asks to commit, save changes to git, or write a commit message.
- figma-spec: Extract a Figma design link into a compact local spec (layout, sizes, colors, typography, borders, radii, shadows, screenshots) mapped to the repo's design-system tokens, saved under docs/design/ so agents can build components without calling Figma again. Use when the user shares a Figma URL, asks to "read/inspect/extract the design", or when building or checking a component against Figma and no local spec exists yet.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

1	# Car Rental UI — Technical Assessment
2	
3	Welcome! This is a hands-on technical assessment. You'll build two React components
4	that render car rental search results, using the provided design system and sample
5	data. Read this whole document before you start.
6	
7	## What we're looking for
8	
9	We care about **how** you build as much as **what** you build: clean, readable code;
10	thoughtful component structure; attention to detail against the designs; and tests
11	you'd be proud to ship. There's no single "right" answer — show us your judgment.
12	
13	## The task
14	
15	Build two Storybook components that match the designs:
16	
17	1. **Car Block** — a single car result card (vehicle details, pricing, policies).
18	2. **Car List** — a list of `Car Block`s rendered from the sample data.
19	
20	Both components must be **responsive** across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
21	
22	## Designs
23	
24	The source of truth for layout, spacing, and styling is Figma:
25	
26	- [CarTrawler Technical Assessment — Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/JlbW0v2Tmf6kybsOEFyhGx/CarTrawler-Technical-Assesment?node-id=10308-24250&t=JXUySO69t2VzVSnO-0)
27	
28	Open the frames in Figma and inspect the elements to understand exactly which token
29	to use for each property (color, font size, spacing, border radius, etc.). Don't guess
30	values — read them off the design.
31	
32	## Design system
33	
34	All styling should come from the design system, not ad-hoc values:
35	
36	- Use the **CSS variables** and **utility classes** defined in
37	  [`src/design-system.css`](./src/design-system.css).
38	  - Color tokens: `--text-*`, `--bg-fill-*`, `--border-*`, `--button-*`, `--price-*`, etc.
39	  - Typography classes: `.ts-display-*`, `.ts-headline-*`, `.ts-subtitle-*`, `.ts-body-*`, `.ts-label-*`, `.ts-button-*`
40	  - Spacing / sizing tokens: `--space-*`, `--bw-*` (border width), `--br-*` (border radius)
41	  - Breakpoints: `--breakpoint-mobile` (608px), `--breakpoint-tablet` (840px), `--breakpoint-desktop-small` (1025px), `--breakpoint-desktop-large` (1328px)
42	- Inspect the elements in Figma to map each visual property to the correct token.
43	- Prefer referencing tokens (`var(--token)` or the `.ts-*` classes) over hard-coded
44	  pixel/hex values so the components stay consistent with the brand.
45	
46	## Sample data

54	Model your TypeScript types around this shape. The **Car List** should render every
55	car in the fixture; the **Car Block** should render a single one.

Checked against `INSTRUCTIONS.md` and the ADR. One item can't be signed off by me: "matches the design".

## Requirements checklist (INSTRUCTIONS.md)

| # | Requirement | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Car Block** matches the design | ⚠️ **Not verifiable** | Figma wasn't exportable, so I built from 5 screenshots plus the nearest tokens. The spec records assumptions A1–A30. The card border colour and the Select's horizontal padding are guesses. QA is still `AWAITING HUMAN APPROVAL`. |
| 2 | **Car List** renders the full set | ✅ | `CarList` renders a `<ul>` with one `<li>` per car. `searchResponse.ts` is the only file that imports the JSON, and the fixture has 5 cars. The list test covers this. |
| 3 | Both **responsive** | ⚠️ **Partly** | There are `min-width` queries at 400, 700 and 870px, so the layouts exist. Those values are temporary and **don't match** the design-system breakpoints (608/840/1025/1328px). |
| 4 | Styling uses **design-system tokens** | ✅ with caveats | A grep found no hex, px or rem literals in the CSS apart from the `@media` conditions. Caveats: Large and XL titles borrow `--space-250` and `--space-400`, and I added `--font-size-subtitle-s` and `--line-height-subtitle-s` to `design-system.css` with your approval. All of this is in `NOTES.md`. |
| 5 | **Stories** for each component | ✅ | CarBlock has 15 stories: sizes, free cancellation vs fee, no insurance, missing and broken image, long name, no rates, and more. CarList has 9: viewports, empty, loading, error and mixed edge cases. The Badge sub-feature has 4. |
| 6 | **Unit tests** colocated | ✅ | 14 test files, 62 tests, all passing. Each component and helper has its own. |
| 7 | **`AGENTS.md`** at the root | ✅ | It's tracked in git and in sync with `CLAUDE.md`. |
| 8 | `lint` and `test` pass | ✅ | Lint is clean and all 62 tests pass. |

## Submission checklist and ADR extras

- ✅ `npm run build` passes.
- ✅ Agent files are committed, and `node_modules`, `dist` and `storybook-static` are not tracked.
- ✅ Accessibility:
  - `<article>` with `aria-labelledby`
  - meaningful `alt` text, with `loading="lazy"` on the car and vendor images
  - focus-visible outlines
  - a rating `aria-label`
  - `aria-busy` on the loading state
- ✅ The loading, empty and error states exist as stories.
- ⚠️ **Coverage:** the 80% target in the QA agent is unmeasured, because `@vitest/coverage-v8` isn't installed.

## Gaps, ranked

1. **Design fidelity:** only you can confirm it against Figma.
2. **Breakpoints:** the code has 400/700/870px. The ADR, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the plan and the spec all say 608/840/1025px. Either swap the code back to the design-system values or update the docs. Left as is, the docs contradict the code. I recommend deciding this before you submit.
3. **Free cancellation:** the fixture has no free cancellation, so that badge can only be seen in Storybook. This is disclosed in `NOTES.md`.
4. **`format:check`:** it fails on 5 files. The untouched ones are `INSTRUCTIONS.md`, the figma-spec skill's two files, `response.json` and `design-system.css`. I'd leave all of them alone, since `response.json` and `design-system.css` are fixtures or source of truth. The `design-system.css` failure is probably my added variables, so I'll check that if you want.
5. **Cosmetic:**
   - Sub-components are still named `CarBlockBadge` and so on, instead of `Badge`.
   - The helper-import rule is still open.

Which do you want to tackle first? My suggestion is the breakpoints (item 2), then installing the coverage package.
